note: Family float resort on the Niangua River near Eldridge: canoe, kayak and raft trips, a waterslide, playgrounds, cabins and a store. The RV sites are on an open field well back from the river, with woods and the primitive tent area between; several electric + water sites come with a gazebo. Water at sites 21-38 is on a well put in in July 2024 (the operator recommends a pressure regulator). Coolers over 48 quarts, styrofoam and glass are not allowed. Primitive tent camping is priced per person. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the operator's page: electric $35, electric + water $40 for up to 6, +$10 per extra person a night (now in fees.extra_person); 30/50A; showers, store, dump station; FareHarbor booking, one night sold, 7 nights max per booking. Under the $50 gate; presence passes (own site with phone and prices; Google 4.7/409). Not seasonal/long-stay. Not waterfront kept (RV field 120-250 m from the Niangua behind woods). Season not stated.
flags: GATE FACTS: posted rate $35 (electric) / $40 (electric + water) a night including 6 people, operator page © 2026 - under US$50, no per-person entry charge on campers (the $10 per person applies to primitive tent camping and to guests past six). PRESENCE: operator website with phone 417-426-5641, prices and a FareHarbor engine. GOOGLE: 4.7 from 409 reviews ('Mountain Creek Family Resort and Canoe Rental LLC', 11564 Kinfolk Rd; phone and website match). RV LIFE: not re-read this pass (stored evidence says unrated, 26 sites; the entry has no rating group). Good Sam: not checked. Reviews were not opened (no borderline call to decide).

LONG-STAY / FLOAT-GROUP: no weekly, monthly or seasonal rates are marketed anywhere on the site or the engine; FareHarbor sells 1-7 nights. It is a float-trip and family-activity resort (waterslide, day passes, pavilions, 20 cabins), so summer weekends will be busy and group-oriented, but nothing reads as residential. Occupancy check, as far as the engine allows: for Friday 2026-11-13 the electric-only item showed bookable_capacity 8, reserved 0 (the map draws 8 electric-only sites: 7-11, 19-21). 2027 weeknights could not be probed - no 2027 calendar is loaded.

MINIMUM STAY: FareHarbor headlines say '2 - 7 Day Rentals' / 'Duration 2 - 7 Days', but the bookable options run 'One Night' to 'Seven Nights' and a single Friday night was offered, so no standing minimum is recorded. Not tested on a summer weekend (no 2027 dates).

SEASON not written: the operator states only store hours ('April 15 through September 30') - not a campground season. FareHarbor sold electric-only sites on November 2026 weekends (to Nov 29) and nothing in December; the electric + water item had no November dates (water presumably off). 2027 not loaded.

FIT: no rig-length figure anywhere (page, map, FareHarbor). The RV sites are back-in pads on an open mown field along gravel loops (map: 37 numbered 'RV/Camper Sites'; imagery shows open ground), so a 23-ft motorhome fits; no posted limit, no 4WD or ford wording (the map marks 'To Prosperine Access' and 'Lebanon' on the county road). sites.count not written: the map numbers sites 1-37 but I could find only 36 of them on it, and the camping page speaks of 'sites 21-38'.
HOOKUPS: stored water:true confirmed (electric + water sites); electric 50 added from the FareHarbor item text ('30 & 50amp plug in'). Sewer not stated (a dump station is on the map).

WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. The water is the Niangua River ('stretching for over half a mile along the pristine, spring-fed Niangua River') - not the Osage Fork. On imagery the RV field's nearest edge is ~120 m from the river and most sites 150-250 m, with a continuous wooded belt between; the operator's map puts only 'Primitive Tent Camping' along the river. The operator's 'great access of the river' wording for the electric sites is access, not frontage. The pond in the field is under an acre.
